title: IAM Access Analyzer Findings

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudwatch:events` events with `detail-type="Access Analyzer Finding" detail.status="ACTIVE"` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.74 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudwatch:events` traffic without `detail-type="Access Analyzer Finding" detail.status="ACTIVE"`. Confirm UC-4.1.74 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch:events` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:events" detail-type="Access Analyzer Finding" detail.status="ACTIVE"
| table _time detail-type source detail.eventName
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.74_iam_access_analyzer_find_74"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.1.74 — IAM Access Analyzer Findings: queries AWS `aws:cloudwatch:events` for search criteria `detail-type="Access Analyzer Finding" detail.status="ACTIVE"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On AWS, detecting 'IAM Access Analyzer Findings' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.1.74 drives medium-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Enable organization-wide analyzer. Send findings to EventBridge and Splunk. Auto-remediate public S3 where policy allows or ticket owners. Weekly review of new external access paths.
visualization: Table (resource type, account, public), Bar chart (findings by type), Single value (active findings).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Alerts.Alerts
  where match(Alerts.app, "(?i)access.analyzer|iam") OR match(Alerts.signature, "(?i)external|public|access")
  by Alerts.severity Alerts.src span=1h
| sort -count

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch:events`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `detail-type` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable organization-wide analyzer. Send findings to EventBridge and Splunk. Auto-remediate public S3 where policy allows or ticket owners. Weekly review of new external access paths.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:events" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:events" detail-type="Access Analyzer Finding" detail.status="ACTIVE"
| table _time detail-type source detail.eventName
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.74_iam_access_analyzer_find_74"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch:events` in `index=aws` to detect iam access analyzer findings. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `detail-type` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_74_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (resource type, account, public), Bar chart (findings by type), Single value (active findings)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of iam access analyzer findings so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
